summary: This week's technology highlights cover breakthroughs and challenges in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity threats, changes in web hosting platforms, and evolving cloud infrastructure initiatives.

items.title: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
items.summary: Anthropic warned that AI development is approaching recursive self-improvement capability where models can train themselves. This threshold marks a potential dramatic acceleration in AI capabilities and autonomous model development.

items.title: One of Google’s Android partners turned 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet
items.summary: Google dismantled a backdoor hidden in 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes by manufacturing partner Videostrong Technology. The compromised devices were secretly used for malicious network traffic routing and ad fraud before Google cut ties with the vendor.

items.title: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees
items.summary: Website builder and web hosting platform Squarespace announced workforce reductions impacting 19 percent of its staff. The company stated the job cuts are part of a broader corporate restructuring.

items.title: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping
items.summary: Major news publishers filed lawsuits against privacy-focused web browser maker Brave for allegedly scraping copyrighted content without authorization. The lawsuit claims Brave monetized its search index by selling access to AI developers for model training.

items.title: OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas
items.summary: OpenAI announced its Grid Protectors Program to share energy from data center power infrastructure during extreme weather emergencies. The initiative aims to relieve public grid strain by offering up to 1,000 megawatts back to local communities.
